The tricky ones are constructing partials with overlapping or mismatched duration field types, so I'm considering using the Partial class to build custom field combinations that would trigger those edge cases.

Designing a minimal test double implementing ReadablePartial's required methods...

But building this custom partial is complex, so I'm leaning toward skipping the hardest-to-trigger edge branches entirely, noting them as difficult to reach through the public API rather than guessing at behavior that isn't in the source.

Since there's no mocking library available, I'll need a custom implementation to exercise that branch.

Writing test double class...

Finishing the stub implementation with remaining methods and noting the needed imports from the joda-time package. Now I'm planning test cases for fieldDifference, covering null start, null end, mismatched sizes, and mismatched field types at some index.

For overlapping duration types I'm thinking through whether distinct standard DateTimeFieldTypes can actually share the same duration type, since fieldDifference relies on the real getDurationType() values rather than anything I can fake through a test partial.

I'll include a few of these edge cases alongside valid constructor calls using PeriodType.yearMonthDay(), plus the duration-based and chronology-based constructors.

I'm listing out the many overloaded constructors for Period — covering duration, start/end longs, ReadableInstant pairs, ReadablePartial pairs, ReadableDuration combinations, and Object-based conversions with optional PeriodType and Chronology parameters. Since most of these just delegate to shared logic without unique branching in Period itself, their main value for coverage is exercising the underlying BasePeriod validation paths.

For the accessor methods (getYears through getMillis) I just need simple tests that read back a field value from a period where each index is set.

For withPeriodType, there are two branches to cover: when the requested type matches the period's current type it should return the same instance, and when it differs it should return a new instance — so I'll test calling it on a standard Period.years(5) with the standard type to confirm identity is preserved.

For withFields, withField, and withFieldAdded, I'm checking null-argument handling (null field or null period returns the same instance or throws IllegalArgumentException), and the zero-value shortcut in withFieldAdded that also returns the same instance. When months reach or exceed 12, dividing by 12 can push years nonzero while the remainder determines whether withMonths fires separately. There's a tricky edge case where negative years combined with exactly 12 months can cancel out during adjustment, leaving both years and months at zero and skipping both calls even though the inputs weren't originally zero.

Now I want to sketch concrete test cases: one where only non-year/month fields are set so both calls are skipped, one where years=2 and months=0 to check only years gets applied, and one where years=0 and months=5 to check only months gets applied.
